passage: The rooftop speakers were so loud that Manoj had to shout into Siddharth's ear. Siddharth, who had been laughing too much for an hour, swayed against him and slurred, "Come back to your room, na? Just us." Manoj felt warmth and a jolt of alarm together. Siddharth could barely stand; whatever he meant, he was in no state to mean it. The last metro left in twenty minutes and the group was already collecting bags. Manoj steered him to the water jug. "Not tonight. Ask me tomorrow, when you're sober, if you still want to." Then he found Priya and Ravi, and the three of them walked Siddharth out, took the same metro, and left him at his own door with a glass of water and a text: "Reached? Sleep. Talk tomorrow."

qa.q: How long until the last metro left?
What was Manoj feeling when Siddharth asked him to come back to his room, and why did he say no?
qa.a: He felt warmth and alarm together. He saw that Siddharth could barely stand and could not clearly agree, so he decided it was not right tonight.

qa.q: What could Manoj do the next day?
qa.a: He could check in on Siddharth, and if Siddharth still wants to talk when sober, have an honest conversation about what each of them wants.

qa.q: How might Siddharth feel when he wakes up?
qa.a: He may feel embarrassed, but also safe and cared for, since he was taken home with water and a message rather than taken advantage of.

grounding: At a party where judgement blurs, the protagonist refuses to take advantage of an impaired partner and leaves with friends.

passage:
Pankaj, before you go to that farewell party, let your Francis uncle tell you something from Goa, long ago. I was twenty, and I liked a girl called Lydia from my college. At a beach party we both drank too much feni. By midnight she could hardly stand, laughing, leaning on me, saying she wanted to go somewhere quiet.
One of my friends winked at me. And I'll be honest, for one moment my head was foggy too, and I thought, she's the one asking.
But she couldn't even say my name straight. That is not someone who can agree to anything. So I sat her down on a plastic chair, got her water, and found her roommate, Agnes. The two of us walked her home, and I slept on the porch outside till morning, just in case.
Next day Lydia thanked me, embarrassed. That friend who winked, I stopped drinking with him. So tonight, you keep an eye on your friends, and you all leave together.

qa.q: What did Francis give Lydia after sitting her down?
What was going on in Francis's mind when his friend winked?
qa.a: He felt tempted and foggy from the drink, briefly thinking "she's the one asking", before seeing that Lydia could not agree to anything.

qa.q: What was the turning point in the story, and why was the choice right?
qa.a: Noticing Lydia couldn't say his name straight; since she couldn't clearly agree, he got her water, found Agnes and walked her home safely.

qa.q: How might Lydia have felt the next day?
qa.a: Embarrassed but grateful and safe, knowing Francis protected her instead of taking advantage.

grounding: Shows judgement blurring at a party and the choice never to take advantage of someone impaired, but to get them home with friends.

passage:
The last metro from Saket left at 11:10, and it was 10:48 when Manoj found Ritika on the balcony of Yogesh's cousin's flat, giggling, her words sliding into each other.
"There you are," she said, catching his sleeve. "Let's find an empty room. Come on."
They'd been dating eight months. But tonight she was swaying, and her eyes weren't quite finding his.
"Not tonight," Manoj said gently. "You're really drunk, and I'm not doing anything you can't properly say yes to. Let's get you home."
She pouted, then sat down hard on a plant pot. He texted Yogesh: "Leaving now. Help?" Yogesh appeared with her bag and a bottle of water.
With twelve minutes left, they half-walked, half-carried her down three floors. On the metro she fell asleep on Manoj's shoulder. Yogesh stayed with them all the way to her PG, and Manoj waited until her roommate opened the door.

qa.q: When did the last metro from Saket leave?
Why did Manoj say "Not tonight" even though they had been dating eight months?
qa.a: He felt protective and cared about Ritika; since she was swaying and couldn't meet his eyes, he knew she could not properly agree.

qa.q: How did Manoj and Yogesh look out for Ritika?
qa.a: They brought her bag and water, got her to the metro together, rode all the way to her PG, and waited until her roommate opened the door.

qa.q: How might Ritika see the night once she is sober?
qa.a: Probably embarrassed but relieved and trusting, knowing Manoj refused to take advantage and made sure she got home safely.

grounding: Illustrates a partner who is impaired at a party and the wise choice to not assume agreement and to leave together with a friend.
